# Final Extreme Execution Graph

The Awtsmoos renews the branch and root, the hidden cause and visible fruit;
Awtsmoos.com shall not be patched by guess, but traced from source to rendered truth.

## Work graph

### A. Whole-repository structural discovery

A1. Census human-authored UI files.
A2. Extract high z-index values and stacking-context creators.
A3. Extract large fixed/min widths and viewport-unit assumptions.
A4. Extract fixed/sticky controls and overflow-clipping ancestors.
A5. Extract responsive breakpoints and mobile-only rules.
A6. Extract dialog/modal/drawer/popover classes and consumers.
A7. Extract canvas/game HUD style ownership.
A8. Extract focus/outline/tabindex patterns.
A9. Cross-map all candidates against git status.
A10. Rank by severity × route fan-out × confidence × cleanliness of ownership.

### B. Readiness-aware runtime proof

B1. Select top risks from each route family.
B2. Start isolated local runtime.
B3. Prove server health before launching Chrome.
B4. Wait until local stylesheets expose parsed CSS rules.
B5. Wait until geometry is stable across consecutive frames.
B6. Measure document and critical-region overflow.
B7. Measure visible control clipping.
B8. Measure fixed/sticky collisions.
B9. Measure 320/390/768/1440 width classes where meaningful.
B10. Repeat at short heights.
B11. Open menus/dialogs/drawers/settings intentionally.
B12. Test focus path on repaired candidates.

### C. Defect qualification

A candidate becomes a repair only if at least one is true:

- a primary or common action is unreachable;
- visible interactive content leaves the viewport without an intentional scroll mechanism;
- document overflow is caused by non-world/non-canvas UI;
- open overlay is clipped or layered beneath unrelated content;
- mobile layout retains desktop structural space that harms usability;
- fixed UI materially obscures content or another control;
- critical touch controls are densely undersized in an actual mobile state;
- focus enters hidden/off-canvas UI or cannot reach visible primary actions;
- a shared primitive causes the same real defect on multiple surfaces.

### D. Full-file implementation discipline

D1. Read every proposed target completely.
D2. Read immediate imports/consumers.
D3. Preserve unrelated dirty work.
D4. If touched source exceeds the project size rule, split responsibilities instead of compressing comments or code.
D5. Rewrite complete touched files only.
D6. Use tabs and readable multiline code.
D7. Preserve public selectors/events/storage/API contracts.
D8. Keep the repair local unless evidence proves shared ownership.
D9. Do not add dependencies for layout repairs.
D10. Do not hide geometry failures with global overflow suppression.

### E. Verification graph

E1. Re-read every changed file.
E2. Run syntax and project-specific tests/build.
E3. Repeat exact runtime reproduction state.
E4. Repeat mobile + desktop state.
E5. Check console/network regressions.
E6. Check affected routes for collateral change.
E7. Inspect git diff line-by-line.
E8. Compare planned versus actual.
E9. Search for shadow work created by the repair.
E10. Close only when remaining evidence-backed repair work is empty.

## Current next action

Run the source-wide structural extraction again in a durable, compact summary format so the previous expired command cannot erase evidence. Store the ranked report in this notebook directory, then inspect the highest-severity clean candidates first.
